@graph.name: Vibrotactile stimulation produces localized contralateral somatosensory autofluorescence (assay validation)
@graph.description: Can the ultra-widefield microscope reproduce known somatotopic cortical responses to tactile stimulation, and thereby qualify a session for chemical stimuli?
@graph.nrr:successCriteria: A localized autofluorescence increase in the somatosensory area contralateral to the stimulated limb, at the anatomically expected position.

nrr:applicabilityConditions.anesthesia: 3-4% isoflurane for induction; maintained at 1.25-1.5% during imaging (from trial file names); depth confirmed by loss of righting reflex, ~1 breath per second, no toe-pinch response
nrr:applicabilityConditions.preparation: head-fixed with earbars in a stereotaxic frame (Kopf); heating pad; hair removed with Nair; eye ointment; 1 mL body-temperature sterile saline subcutaneous; 0.1 mL 1% lidocaine subcutaneous under the scalp; scalp removed; periosteum cleaned; thin layer of cyanoacrylate glue applied to the skull for optical clarity
nrr:applicabilityConditions.invasiveness: through-skull, label-free; no craniotomy, no transgenic animals, no dye or virus injection
nrr:applicabilityConditions.readout: flavoprotein autofluorescence, dF/F over a region of interest
nrr:applicabilityConditions.imaging: 10 frames per second, 13.4 x 11.3 mm, 5 um/px with no binning; cropped to the brain and binned 4 x 4 for all trials
nrr:applicabilityConditions.analysis: temporal averaging: 2 frames for tactile trials, 8 frames for injection trials, to reduce noise; motion correction by SIFT-based registration; brain masking by flood fill (scikit-image flood); bleach correction: subtract the bottom 5% of pixels within the brain from each frame; baseline autofluorescence subtraction
nrr:applicabilityConditions.statistics: none reported; no significance testing, no power analysis, no detection limit stated anywhere in the pub

nrr:cost.note: 13 imaging trials across 5 mice. The pub reports the imaging system cost (approximately US$30,000 including the camera) as capital, not as the cost of this study; no per-study cost is given.
nrr:cost.source: Methods, Microscope and sensory stimulation hardware

nrr:provenanceNotes: The troubleshooting loop in this stage means the tactile signal was tuned into existence per session. This does not undermine the positive result, but it is why the tactile response is recorded as an internal positive control for later trials rather than as an independent one.

nrr:aiUseDeclaration.statement: We used ChatGPT to help write and clean up code, and GitHub Copilot to help write and add comments to our code.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.purpose: writing and cleaning up analysis code

nrr:confidence.basis: three trials, consistent with known anatomy and with published flavoprotein imaging, but each n = 1 and obtained after per-trial tuning

@graph.nrr:outcomeSummary: Contralateral, somatotopically appropriate responses for right hindlimb, left hindlimb and right forelimb stimulation; a 1-3% increase in autofluorescence above baseline after averaging 50 stimulations.

complianceIds: All animal work performed in accordance with the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee of the Charles River Accelerator and Development Lab (CRADL, South San Francisco, CA). No protocol number is given in the pub.

@graph.name: vibrating tactile stimulation of a single limb
@graph.nrr:protocol: 50 vibrational pulses, 2 s on, 4 s off, imaged simultaneously at 10 fps

nrr:conditions.stimulator: vibrating motor (Amazon B07Q1ZV4MJ) taped to the paw, driven by a simple circuit on two AA batteries
nrr:conditions.expectation: brain activity in S1 (primary somatosensory area), based on refs 19-20
nrr:conditions.anesthesia: 3-4% isoflurane for induction; maintained at 1.25-1.5% during imaging (from trial file names); depth confirmed by loss of righting reflex, ~1 breath per second, no toe-pinch response

nrr:protocolAdaptations: adjusted the positioning of the stimulator
reduced the isoflurane level by 0.25% (never below 1%)
placed the stimulator on a different limb
@graph.nrr:note: If we didn't detect a cortical response in S1, we performed the following troubleshooting steps and tried again ... In most cases, one or more of these steps resulted in a clear signal. Once we observed a brain response to a tactile stimulus, we proceeded with chemical stimuli. A trial was therefore repeated with adjusted settings until a signal appeared, which means the tactile result is a tuned positive rather than a first-pass one.

@graph.name: imaging analysis pipeline
@graph.nrr:method: temporal averaging: 2 frames for tactile trials, 8 frames for injection trials, to reduce noise; motion correction by SIFT-based registration; brain masking by flood fill (scikit-image flood); bleach correction: subtract the bottom 5% of pixels within the brain from each frame; baseline autofluorescence subtraction
@graph.nrr:note: for visualisation, pixel intensities in vehicle and drug trials were scaled to a shared min and max; dF/F was computed on non-adjusted baseline-subtracted data
